spec: Build an expense-tracking API. Users record expenses with an amount, category and date, list expenses filtered by category or month, and request a summary endpoint that returns total spend per category for a given month. Expenses are stored in DynamoDB.

complexity.rationale: One store, but compound filtering and monthly aggregation make it more than basic CRUD.

congruence_checklist: GET endpoint filtering by category and month
Summary endpoint aggregating spend per category
Expense model has amount, category, date

plan.summary: A JSON REST API for personal expense tracking. Clients create expense records (amount, category, date, optional note), retrieve and delete individual expenses, list expenses filtered by category and/or month, and fetch a per-category spend summary for a given month. All records persist in a single DynamoDB table keyed by user, with a secondary index that supports category-scoped queries; monthly filtering uses the date-prefixed sort key. The service is a standalone FastAPI process (run by the harness) that talks to DynamoDB directly via boto3 — no Lambda, queue or asynchronous processing is implied by the specification.

endpoints.purpose: Liveness/readiness probe that also verifies the DynamoDB table is reachable.
Create a new expense record with amount, category, date and optional description; returns the stored item including its generated id.
List expenses for the caller, optionally filtered by ?category= and/or ?month=YYYY-MM; uses the category GSI when a category is supplied and a sort-key range query for the month.
Retrieve a single expense by its id.
Update the amount, category, date or description of an existing expense.
Return total spend per category (and an overall total) for the month given by the required ?month=YYYY-MM query parameter.

data_models.name: Expense
fields: user_id: string (partition key, from X-User-Id header, default 'default')
amount: decimal (positive, 2dp, stored as DynamoDB Number)
category: string (free-form label, e.g. 'groceries', normalised to lowercase)
month: string (YYYY-MM, derived from date, used for filtering/summaries)
gsi1pk: string ('<user_id>#<category>' for the category index)

data_models.name: ExpenseListResponse
fields: next_cursor: string (optional, base64 LastEvaluatedKey for pagination)

aws_resources.name: expenses
aws_resources.justification: Primary persistence for expense records as explicitly required by the spec. Partition key user_id, sort key sk ('<date>#<expense_id>') so month filtering and summaries are range queries on a date prefix; PAY_PER_REQUEST billing.

aws_resources.name: expenses-gsi-category (GSI on the expenses table)
aws_resources.justification: Global secondary index with partition key gsi1pk ('<user_id>#<category>') and sort key sk, so GET /expenses?category= and the per-category summary can query instead of scanning.

aws_resources.name: expense-tracker-app-role (with expense-tracker-dynamodb-policy)
aws_resources.justification: Least-privilege role/policy granting the backend service GetItem, PutItem, UpdateItem, DeleteItem and Query on the expenses table and its category GSI — the only AWS calls the application makes.

aws_resources.name: /cloudforge/expense-tracker-api (log group)
aws_resources.justification: Destination for the application's structured request/error logs, with a retention period set so operational output is queryable.

assumptions: Multi-tenancy is implied by 'users' but no auth scheme is specified: the caller identity is taken from an X-User-Id request header and defaults to 'default' when absent; no authentication/authorisation layer is generated.

No asynchronous, scheduled or event-driven work is described, so no SQS, SNS, Lambda or API Gateway resources are planned — the FastAPI service is started directly by the harness and calls DynamoDB with boto3.

Amounts are stored as DynamoDB Numbers using Python Decimal to avoid float rounding errors, and a single currency (default USD) is assumed since the spec mentions none; summaries do not perform FX conversion.
'Month' filters and summaries use the calendar month of the expense date in the format YYYY-MM, interpreted in UTC.
Categories are free-form strings normalised to lowercase/trimmed rather than a fixed enum, since the spec defines no category list.
List endpoints return newest-first results with a default page size of 50 (max 200) and an opaque cursor for pagination.
No receipt/file uploads are mentioned, so no S3 bucket is planned; no secrets are required, so Secrets Manager is omitted.
DynamoDB endpoint, region and table name are supplied via environment variables (AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, AWS_REGION, EXPENSES_TABLE) so the service can point at LocalStack.
